rendered: The paper does not give a cost per kWh for the NFA 811[1] pouch cell. The only cost-per-energy figure it states is the general U.S. DOE cell cost target of $80/kWh[2], which is a target, not a measured result for that cell. It says that current manufacturing costs in general are about double that target: "current manufacturing costs are about double this figure[3]". For the cobalt-free NFA cathode, Table 1[4] gives only an estimated energy density improvement of 250–275[5] Wh/kg under Section 7 – Co-Free NFA[6], which is not a cost figure.
